memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: ""Look," he said to his people, "the Israelites have become far too numerous for us. Come, we must deal shrewdly with them or they will become even more numerous and, if war breaks out, will join our enemies, fight against us and leave the country."" - Exodus 1:9-10 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Pharaoh's speech is a study in how fear works. Notice the words: too numerous, if war breaks out, they will join our enemies. None of it had happened. It was all imagination. Yet on the basis of a fear that existed only in his mind, he decided to enslave an entire people.

Fear rarely stays private. It looks for a plan, and the plan usually harms someone. Behind most cruelty in this world — communal, racial, domestic — you will find someone who was afraid and decided to protect himself at another's cost.

This should make us examine our own hearts. What have I said or done recently because I was afraid of losing something? Fear makes us controlling with our children, suspicious of our colleagues, harsh with people who are different from us.

The gospel answers fear at its root. When we know that God is for us and nothing can separate us from His love (Rom 8:31-39), we no longer need to secure ourselves by pushing others down.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What fear is currently shaping how I treat people?
2. Where has my imagination turned someone into an enemy?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, search my heart for the fears I have not admitted. Teach me to trust You so completely that I have no need to harm anyone. Amen.
